name: Riboswitch / RNA Structure Targeting
therapeuticGoalDescription: Modulate translation by stabilizing or destabilizing structured RNA elements (IRES, G-quadruplexes, riboswitches) that control ribosomal entry or scanning.
molecularDefect: Diseases where a structured RNA element aberrantly regulates translation initiation or elongation.
diseaseMechanism: Pathogenic RNA secondary structures (e.g., G-quadruplexes in 5' UTR, IRES elements, riboswitch-like motifs) occlude ribosome scanning or aberrantly recruit translation machinery. ASOs are designed to bind and either stabilize or disrupt these structures, redirecting ribosome access and restoring normal translation levels.
suitableVariantTypes: Variants that create, stabilize, or destabilize structured RNA elements in the 5' UTR, 3' UTR, or coding sequence that alter translation efficiency.
typicalDiseases: Investigational applications in neurodegeneration (G-quadruplex dysregulation), cancer (IRES-driven translation), and rare metabolic disorders with riboswitch-like RNA elements.
rnaTargetRegion: Structured RNA elements: Internal Ribosome Entry Sites (IRES); G-quadruplexes (G4); riboswitch aptamer domains; stem-loop regulatory structures in 5' UTR or CDS.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript containing a validated or predicted structured regulatory RNA element (IRES, G-quadruplex, or riboswitch-like motif) that modulates translation.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs (PMO, 2'-O-MOE, LNA) designed to bind structured elements without degrading the transcript, preserving the mRNA while altering its translational accessibility.
typicalLength: Typically 18-25 nucleotides; longer oligos (20-30 nt) may be required for stable binding to structured targets.
designRules: Literature synthesis: predict and validate secondary structure of the target region; design ASOs complementary to structured elements to either stabilize or disrupt the fold; use RNase H-independent chemistries; confirm structural change via SHAPE-MaP or DMS-MaPseq.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Essential — the target must form a defined secondary or tertiary structure (stem-loop, G-quadruplex, IRES) that the ASO is designed to bind and modulate.
offTargetConsiderations: Structured elements may have paralogous motifs in other transcripts; evaluate genome-wide structural similarity to avoid unintended translation changes.
advantages: Enables precise control of translation through RNA structure modulation; preserves transcript abundance; targets a distinct regulatory layer beyond splicing and coding sequence.
limitations: Requires high-confidence structural annotation of the target RNA; structure prediction tools have limited accuracy for long-range RNA folding; clinical validation is limited.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified. Current applications remain preclinical or proof-of-concept.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic rationale from RNA structure biology; translational therapeutic applications are investigational.

referencesSummary: G4 RNA structure in translation control (Rhodes et al., 2018); IRES-targeting ASOs (Tarasov et al., 2021); riboswitch RNA targeting (Patel et al., 2023).

references.paper: Rhodes JD et al. G-quadruplex RNA structure in translation regulation. Nature Chemical Biology (2018)
